newsitem.title: USA: Emery pilots vote in favor of union.
newsitem.headline: Emery pilots vote in favor of union.

text.p: The cockpit crew members of Emery Worldwide Airlines have voted for union representation, the Air Line Pilots Association said Thursday.
The union said that of the 348 pilots eligible to participate, 64 percent, or 223, voted in favor of the union.
Emery spokesman Rocco Sacci said it is the first time Emery's pilots have been unionized since the company was founded.

"We have a consistent and longstanding history of very positive relations with our employees, and our opinion is bringing in a third party is unnecessary. However we don't anticipate any impact on our daily operations or on the future growth of the company," Sacci said.
Sacci said the company would offer no other statement on the matter.
ALPA spokesman John Mazor said terms of what the pilots will ask for has yet to be determined.
"It's going to be a while before the pilots are in a position to approach the company and ask to begin negotiations for their first labor contract," Mazor said.
Emery, a division of CNF Transportation Inc, is headquartered in Redwood City, California, and provides overnight package express, freight forwarding and charter services.
The division generated nearly $2 billion of the nearly $3.7 billion in revenues reported by CNF in 1996.
